newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - Oct 17.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - Oct 17.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN
After a three-year absence, the Queensland Women's Tennis Open is back on the Australian calendar and set to trial the new Lykold Grand Slam court surface for Tennis Australia. Page 20.

The long-running dispute between SKY Channel and TABCORP, which has seen Victorian TAB outlets without race pictures for more than two weeks, will be resolved in time for the Caulfield Cup meeting after the formal exchanging of letters this morning betwee the two companies. Page 22.

Former slow bowler Terry Jenner says leg-spinner Shane Warne has the capacity to be a future Test captain, but in the interim Australia needs to closely monitor his recovery from surgery on his injured spinning finger. Page 22.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Having earlier agreed to a two-year coaching deal with Japanese J-League club Sanfrecce Hiroshima, Eddie Thompson met Soccer Australia chairman David Hill yesterday afternoon and quit as national coach of the Socceroos, ending a turbulent six-year reign. Page 48.

Furious Netball Australia executives have vowed to fight the Australian Sports Commission Board's move to cut the funding of the A$473,000 Australian Institute of Sport residential netball program, which will go unless the AIS has a side in the new eight-team national competition. Page 48.
The Australian Rugby League finals draw has been heavily criticised by Super League proponents who claim teams would be better off losing their first-week finals match. Page 48.
THE AGE

According to the AFL players' association's executive director, Peter Allen, one AFL player is believed to have tested positive for marijuana use this season, following the testing of 176 players. Page C14.

Former North Melbourne Giants import Paul Maley may reject the basketball club's offer to work in its offices for one year before returning to play as an Australian in 1998, with his first priority being to play next season despite the back injury that kept him out of the quarter-final series. Page C14.

After winning the Caulfield Guineas with Alfa last Saturday, master trainer Bart Cummings won his fourth Thousand Guineas when the brilliant Dashing Eagle charged away for an easy win in yesterday's group one classic at Caulfield. Page C16.
HERALD SUN
Socceroo striker Joe Spiteri has accepted a trial with UK soccer club Queens Park Rangers and will play tonight in a testimonial match to give the team a chance to look at him. Page 87.

Cycling officials considered cancelling yesterday afternoon's criterium stage of the VicHealth Herald Sun Tour after drenching rain made the circuit treacherous, but the stage went ahead with American Scott Moninger increasing his overnight lead by five sconds over Australian Stephen Hodge. Page 90.
AFL Premier North Melbourne yesterday de-listed Keenan Reynolds, who originally priced himself at more than A$100,000 to get to Arden Street. Page 94.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

According to a summons filed in the New South Wales Industrial Court yesterday, leading rugby league coach Phil Gould "unfairly" persuaded Penrith's John Cartwright to sign an Australian Rugby League loyalty agreement during a judiciary appearance at ARL headquarters last year. Page 94.

The financially embattled South Queensland Crushers rugby league club was yesterday saved from extinction for at least two weeks after an arrangement was made with the Commonwealth Bank over outstanding debts. Page 94.

Champion jockey Mick Dittman is in danger of losing the Cox Plate ride on Filante after the shock defeat of 5/4 favourite Filante under controversial circumstances sparked a noisy and prolonged demonstration at Caulfield yesterday. Page 96.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
